title: The Lebesgue and Riemann Integrals Compared

items.title: A bounded Riemann integrable function admits Borel Darboux envelopes with zero integral gap
items.strategy: Choose a nested sequence of partitions whose upper and lower Darboux sums converge to the common Riemann value. The associated lower and upper step functions are Borel, monotone under refinement, and have Lebesgue integrals equal to those Darboux sums. Their pointwise supremum and infimum are therefore Borel envelopes with integral gap zero.

items.title: A bounded Riemann integrable function on a closed bounded interval is Lebesgue measurable and has the same integral
items.strategy: Use the Borel Darboux envelopes from the preceding lemma. Their difference has nonnegative integral zero, so they agree almost everywhere; the bounded function between them is therefore almost everywhere equal to a Borel function and is measurable because Lebesgue measure is complete. Boundedness on a finite interval gives integrability, and almost-everywhere equality identifies the Lebesgue integral with the common Darboux-Riemann value.

items.title: A Riemann integrable function on a closed bounded interval is almost everywhere equal to a Borel function
items.strategy: The envelope lemma already produces Borel lower and upper envelopes whose difference has integral zero. The zero-integral criterion makes the envelopes equal almost everywhere, and the original function lies between them, so it agrees almost everywhere with either Borel envelope.

items.title: Arzela's bounded convergence theorem for Riemann integrals
items.strategy: Convert each Riemann integrable function, and the Riemann integrable pointwise limit, into Lebesgue-integrable functions with the same values on the same interval. The common uniform bound makes the sequence dominated by an integrable constant on a finite-measure space, so bounded convergence gives convergence of the Lebesgue integrals, hence of the Riemann integrals.

items.title: A nonnegative improper Riemann integral on a half-line agrees with the Lebesgue integral
items.strategy: For $R > a$, truncate $f$ to $[a,R]$. Each truncation is Riemann integrable and therefore Lebesgue integrable with the same value on that compact interval. The truncations increase pointwise to $f$, so monotone convergence passes the Lebesgue integrals to the limit, which is exactly the improper Riemann integral when that finite limit exists.

items.title: For a continuous integrand, the Riemann-Stieltjes and Lebesgue-Stieltjes integrals agree
items.strategy: Let $F$ be nondecreasing and right-continuous on $\mathbb{R}$, with Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure $\mu_F$. A continuous integrand on $[a,b]$ is Borel measurable, and the lower and upper Stieltjes sums for a partition are exactly the Lebesgue integrals of the associated lower and upper step functions over $(a,b]$, because $\mu_F((x_{i-1},x_i]) = F(x_i)-F(x_{i-1})$. The Stieltjes Darboux criterion squeezes the Lebesgue-Stieltjes integral between those sums and forces equality with the mesh-limit Riemann-Stieltjes integral.

title: The Lebesgue and Riemann Integrals Compared — Examples

items.title: The indicator of the rationals in $[0,1]$ is Lebesgue integrable with integral $0$ and not Riemann integrable
items.strategy: Use the published continuity-set description of the Dirichlet function together with the nullity of countable sets, the zero-a.e. criterion for the Lebesgue integral, and Lebesgue's criterion for Riemann integrability. This gives the side-by-side comparison without appealing to a separate examples page.

items.title: FALSE: every Riemann integrable function on a closed bounded interval is Borel measurable
items.strategy: Rebuild the MT-5 Hunter witness: choose a nonmeasurable subset $N$ of the positive-measure compact image $\psi[C]$ of the Cantor set and pull it back through $\psi(x)=x+c(x)$ to a Lebesgue measurable non-Borel set $E\subseteq C$. The indicator $\mathbf{1}_E$ on $[0,1]$ is continuous off the closed Cantor set, so its discontinuity set lies in the Lebesgue-null set $C$ and the published Lebesgue criterion makes it Riemann integrable. If $\mathbf{1}_E$ were Borel measurable, then $E=\mathbf{1}_E^{-1}((1/2,\infty))$ would be Borel in $[0,1]$, hence Borel in $\mathbb{R}$ by the subspace-trace theorem since $[0,1]$ is closed, contradiction.

items.title: An open dense set of measure less than $1$ is the monotone $L^1$-limit of Riemann integrable indicators, but its indicator is not Riemann integrable
items.strategy: Enumerate $\mathbb Q\cap(0,1)$ and surround its $k$th term by an open interval of length at most $2^{-k-3}$. Their union $U$ is open and dense, while countable subadditivity and the geometric series give $\lambda(U)<1$. Let $U_n$ be the union of the first $n$ intervals. Each indicator $\mathbf 1_{U_n}$ has only finitely many discontinuities, the sequence increases pointwise to $\mathbf 1_U$, and continuity from below gives $L^1$ convergence. Since $U$ is dense and its positive-measure complement is closed, $\partial U$ has positive measure, so the Lebesgue criterion rules out Riemann integrability of $\mathbf 1_U$.

items.title: The sine integral is improperly Riemann integrable and not Lebesgue integrable
items.strategy: Use Dirichlet's test to obtain convergence of the improper integral of sin x / x, and use the published uniform-tail-mass criterion to show that its absolute integral diverges. Then the Lebesgue integral does not exist although the improper Riemann integral does.

items.title: The indicator of a fat Cantor set is upper semicontinuous and equal almost everywhere to no Riemann integrable function
items.strategy: Take the indicator of the Smith-Volterra-Cantor set. Closed-set indicators are upper semicontinuous, and the set has positive measure. If a function agrees with this indicator almost everywhere, then its disagreement set is null; every neighborhood of every point of the positive-measure set left after removing that null set still contains points outside the Cantor set and outside the null set, so the modified function remains discontinuous on a positive-measure set and cannot be Riemann integrable.

items.title: A null set can fail to be the discontinuity set of any function
items.strategy: Enumerate the rationals as $(q_j)$. For each $k$, let $U_k$ be the union of intervals about $q_j$ whose lengths sum to at most $2^{-k}$. Each $U_k$ is open and dense, and $G=\bigcap_k U_k$ is therefore a dense $G_\delta$ by Baire; monotonicity gives $\lambda(G)\le 2^{-k}$ for every $k$, hence $G$ is null. If $G$ were a function's discontinuity set, the $F_\sigma$ theorem would write it as a countable union of closed null sets. Each has empty interior, making $G$ meager, while its dense $G_\delta$ presentation makes it residual, a contradiction to Baire category.
